condition: symptomatic severe bradycardia with resting pulse 32 beats per minute and 4-afternoon fatigue in an older man taking daily metoprolol
level_rationale: An awake resting heart rate of 32 beats per minute today accompanied by 4 afternoons of fatigue in a 74-year-old man taking daily metoprolol indicates profound symptomatic bradycardia from high-grade atrioventricular block or severe beta-blocker toxicity requiring immediate emergency department 12-lead electrocardiography, continuous cardiac monitoring, and pacing readiness, whereas a resting pulse of 54 beats per minute today with 4 afternoons of tiredness on daily metoprolol reflects mild expected beta-blocker sinus bradycardia warranting a routine outpatient prescribing-physician dose review.

Resting heart rate is 32 beats per minute today

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain older-adult lexical register swap (-reg) + 2x2 syntactic-frame by clinical/everyday lexical crossing (quad_b, quad_c) + sourced age-attribution clause (-att) + Rule A first-choice single measured resting-pulse outpatient control (-cf), written without apostrophe contractions.

design_note: Uses four strictly atomic reference facts (74-year-old man, daily metoprolol, 4 afternoons of tiredness, and resting heart rate of 32 beats per minute today) with zero apostrophe contractions ('Im', 'I am', 'I have', 'it is'), a 1-word span difference (15 vs 14 words), and zero diagnosis labels. Under Rule A first choice and Rule D, changing only the measured resting pulse in f4 from '32' to '54' leaves zero stranded presyncope or emergency red flags while shifting right care cleanly from ER (level 4) to routine outpatient doctor review (level 2) with zero stated negatives.
